v4_prefix_invariant.claim: v5_input[:52] is byte-identical to the V4 input vector, in the V4 order, produced by the unmodified V4 code

fragmentation.note: Implemented per RFC 791 / RFC 8200 and verified against synthetic first / middle / last / IPv6-fragment-header fixtures. IDENTICALLY ZERO in every capture available to this project (0 fragments in 303,922 real IP packets), so two of its three features carry no variance here. Reported, not hidden, and not downgraded to a pass by pretending the data supports it.

retransmission.note: Measures sequence-space re-coverage = retransmission + genuine reordering. The two are not separable without RTT and duplicate-ACK context. Zero-length packets are excluded, so duplicate ACKs are never counted.

formulas.ttl_mean: float(ttl.mean()) over every IP packet whose timestamp falls in [t, t+10)
formulas.ttl_min: float(ttl.min()) over every IP packet whose timestamp falls in [t, t+10)
formulas.ttl_max: float(ttl.max()) over every IP packet whose timestamp falls in [t, t+10)
formulas.log_tcp_window_mean: _safe_log1p(win.mean()) where win = raw 16-bit TCP window of every TCP packet in [t, t+10)
formulas.log_tcp_window_max: _safe_log1p(win.max()) over the raw window field of every TCP packet in [t, t+10)
formulas.tcp_window_change_rate: _ratio(n_win_changed, n_win_eligible) where a packet is 'eligible' iff it is TCP and not the first packet of its directional session (ordered 5-tuple, 120 s idle reset), and 'changed' iff its raw window value differs from that predecessor's
formulas.frag_packet_ratio: _ratio(n_frag, n_ip) — fragmented IP packets over all IP packets in [t, t+10)
formulas.ip_df_ratio: _ratio(n_df, n_ip4) — the denominator is IPv4 packets ONLY
formulas.log_tcp_retrans_count: _safe_log1p(sum(is_retransmission)); is_retransmission is True iff the packet is TCP, eff_len = payload_len + (1 if SYN) + (1 if FIN) > 0, the packet is not the first seq-bearing packet of its directional session, and seq + eff_len is at or below that session's running high-water mark under 32-bit modular comparison
formulas.payload_len_max: float(payload_len.max()) over every IP packet in [t, t+10)
formulas.payload_len_entropy: -sum(p * log2(p + 1e-12)) over value_counts(payload_len) / total; 0.0 when <= 1 distinct length. Identical formula to the V4 dst_port_entropy / protocol_entropy.

relative_change.rule: explicit per-feature ruling; see docs/v5_packet_feature_contract.json features[].relative_change_decision / relative_change_reason

packet_parity.basis: one shared implementation (src/packet_feature_builder.py) for both the training-side and the PCAP-side entry point, verified numerically across two independent invocation routes (in-memory vs CSV round-trip + shuffle)
packet_parity.caveat: This proves the two ROUTES agree and that no plumbing drift exists. It does not — and cannot — prove agreement with a second independent packet feature implementation, because no such implementation exists: the training data is flow CSVs with no packet fields at all.

conformance.note: The five demo captures are synthetically generated and have constant TTL (64) and constant TCP window (8192), so several packet features are necessarily constant on them. That is a property of those files, not of the features — the real capture shows 67 distinct TTLs and 1,399 distinct window values. No capture here is used for training.

leakage_checks.definition: every packet contributes only to the window containing its own timestamp, [t, t+10)
rebuilding from a strict prefix of the capture leaves every already-completed window bit-identical — the decisive test that no future packet edits a past state
each relative change uses the immediately preceding EXISTING row and nothing else; first row forced to 0.0

packet features are assigned PER PACKET, not per flow, so a flow that continues past t+10 contributes to the later window only. This is the structural difference from the V4 flow lane, where a whole flow is attributed to the window of its first packet.
leakage_checks.result: PASS — by construction, and confirmed by prefix_truncation_invariance

leakage_checks.definition: annotate_packets is a single forward pass in timestamp order; every annotation is written once and never revised

v5_training_dataset_verdict.reason: The three TRAIN/VAL days (Wednesday-14-02-2018, Thursday-15-02-2018, Wednesday-28-02-2018) have ZERO packet captures on disk. Only the pre-computed CICFlowMeter flow CSVs were ever obtained for them, and a flow CSV cannot yield TTL, TCP window, IP fragment flags or TCP sequence numbers — those fields do not exist in it at any aggregation level. Even the TEST day (Friday-02-03-2018) has only 20 of 440 host captures on disk, so its packet coverage is a partial-scope subset rather than the whole monitored organisation the flow CSV aggregates.

A_reprocess_original_pcaps.detail: There are no original PCAPs for the three train/val days to reprocess. For 02-03 the source archive is 41.7 GiB compressed / 54.7 GB uncompressed against ~49 GB free disk, and downloading it would still leave train and val empty.

B_join_packet_features_where_pcap_exists.detail: Would populate packet features on the TEST day only and leave them structurally missing on every TRAIN and VAL window. A model cannot learn a feature it never sees in training, and filling the gap with zeros or means would be exactly the unsupported imputation Part 17 forbids — it would also make the packet block a perfect test-set indicator, which is a leakage channel, not a feature.

C_packet_features_for_pcap_demonstration.detail: The chosen option. The packet lane is fully built, contracted, tested and verified, and runs on real captures. It is used for PCAP-side analysis and conformance now; no V5 model is trained.

D_retrain_the_flow_lane_from_pcap_for_al.detail: Would require the full 440-host archive for all four days — three of which were never captured to disk at all — plus a re-derivation of the labels, and would change the flow features too, destroying the controlled V4-vs-V5 comparison Part 23 requires.

what_would_unblock_it: Packet captures for Wednesday-14-02-2018, Thursday-15-02-2018 and Wednesday-28-02-2018 at the monitored-organisation scope the flow CSVs cover.
Enough disk (~55 GB per day, or a batch extract-fold-delete loop) to process them.
A re-derivation of the 26 flow features from those same captures, so that flow and packet features share one capture scope instead of the current hybrid.

v5_model_reason: Part 22 forbids training until a training, validation AND test set with populated packet features all exist. Train and val have zero packet captures, so the prerequisite fails and training was not attempted. No V5 checkpoint, config, scaler or prediction file was created.

hybrid_representation.flow_features: APPROXIMATE relative to CICFlowMeter training semantics — the Task 7 finding is preserved unchanged, not re-litigated
hybrid_representation.packet_features: DIRECT — computed from packet timestamps and header fields, with no flow-engine intermediary
hybrid_representation.claim_limit: No claim of full numerical equivalence with CICFlowMeter is made anywhere. V5 is explicitly a hybrid representation.

unsupported_features.reason: a defensible duplicate-ACK rule needs the ACK number plus SACK-option parsing; the parser does not read TCP options, so the rule would be approximate. Deferred rather than shipped weak.
requires RTT estimation and duplicate-ACK context. The shipped feature is documented as sequence-space re-coverage instead of being mislabelled a pure retransmission count.
the scale factor is only observable when the SYN handshake is inside the capture, which is false for mid-capture connections. The raw header value is used consistently instead.

remaining_limitations: The three TRAIN/VAL benchmark days have NO packet captures at all, so no V5 training dataset exists and no V5 model was trained.
IP fragmentation is identically zero in every capture available here, so log_frag_packet_count and frag_packet_ratio are implemented and fixture-verified but carry no variance in this data.
The retransmission family measures sequence-space re-coverage, which is retransmission plus genuine reordering; the two are not separable without RTT and duplicate-ACK context.
TCP window values are raw header units; the window-scale option is not applied.
The V4 flow lane remains APPROXIMATE relative to CICFlowMeter training semantics (Task 7 finding, unchanged). V5 is therefore a HYBRID: approximate flow features plus direct packet features.
